{"code": "import pandas as pd

data = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Confirm that the duplicates are exactly 48 patients with two rows each
# and that the higher sample_seq row is the one to keep
duplicate_patients = data[data['patient_id'].duplicated(keep=False)]

# Group by patient_id and find the max sample_seq for each
max_sample_seq_per_patient = duplicate_patients.groupby('patient_id')['sample_seq'].max()

# Check if all duplicates have exactly two rows and the max sample_seq is 2
# (i.e., they have both sample_seq 1 and 2)
duplicate_counts = duplicate_patients['patient_id'].value_counts()
print(f'Number of patients with multiple rows: {len(duplicate_counts)}')
print(f'All duplicates have exactly 2 rows: {all(duplicate_counts == 2)}')

# Now deduplicate: keep the row with the highest sample_seq per patient
deduplicated_data = data.loc[data.groupby('patient_id')['sample_seq'].idxmax()]

# Final number of unique patients
num_patients = len(deduplicated_data)
print(f'Number of unique patients after deduplication: {num_patients}')"}
